hooks.command: r=("STOP-GATE: Name the single highest-leverage unfinished change toward the end-state (no bounds / one scheduler / universal heap-switch). Did this turn advance it via ANY of: a moved metric, a verified capability, a decisive measurement that PICKED or REDIRECTED the next build, or the exact next diff named? If yes you may stop clean. If you only banked verified work, deferred to a fresh session, or repeated a known fact to avoid the hard build, that is the fake end — go build it." "STOP-GATE: Reverting a CORRECT change to dodge a regression or to wait for a fresh session is the banned move — fix forward. But reverting a change that crashes/loops/regresses the moat (one YOU just broke) is correct hygiene, not a stall — never sit on a broken change to satisfy this gate. Say honestly which you did." "STOP-GATE: Planning and measurement ARE expected for the best design — a signal that redirects the build, or a plan naming the exact next diff, is progress, not stalling. The addiction traps are: flat with NO named next diff, and repeated banking. State the next diff in one sentence; if the turn advanced the design and you can, stop clean." "STOP-GATE: Did you fake-end? 'restore the moat to working state', 'won't ship at the tail of a long session', 'let me strip the diagnostics', or bank verified work to dodge the hard rearchitecture are the dodges to catch. Measuring to pick the right target, or naming a located next diff, is NOT a dodge. Do the hard thing if it is in reach this turn; else name it precisely and stop." "STOP-GATE: Name the riskiest valuable action you are avoiding because it might break the build or regress a number. If you dodged it for a safe edge-diff, switch to it. If you DID it and it broke, fix forward or revert-the-broken honestly — do not keep a crash to look busy."); printf '{"decision":"block","reason":"%s"}' "${r[$((RANDOM % ${#r[@]}))]}"

r=("POST-EDIT CHECK: Was this the core mechanism, or adjacent work (tooling/logging/comment/test)? Adjacent is legitimate ONLY when it unblocks the core (a signal or build flag you genuinely need next). If it is polishing edges while the located hard change waits, switch to the hard one." "POST-EDIT CHECK: If this reverts a CORRECT change to dodge a regression, undo the dodge and fix the root. If it reverts a change YOU just broke (crash/loop/moat regression), that is correct — but do not stop there, name and pursue the real fix." "POST-EDIT CHECK: Does this move toward deleting a bound, collapsing to one scheduler, and universal heap-switching? Verify on the live Chrome harness, not by reasoning." "POST-EDIT CHECK: Name the single next edit toward the end-state. A measurement or a plan counts if it picks that edit; a flat edge-edit with no next step does not."); printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"%s"}}' "${r[$((RANDOM % ${#r[@]}))]}"

echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"No short term thinking. Provide balanced feedback both negative and positive; ask why questions to learn the intent. Planning and measurement are expected for the best design; gaming the gate with fake end-turns is not."}}'
